attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, presented as his assessment of Anthropic.

semantics.note: Two parts. 'Reasons to believe things have gotten worse' is hedged and not scored. 'The fact that it has resorted to adjusted margins... faking a profit in Q3 2026' is a firm factual assertion. The normalisation keeps both parts and their modalities.

contract.note: Scoring the firm core is fair: Q3 profit claimed on an adjusted basis that hides a loss. The result depends on how 'faking' and 'adjusted margins' are read against adjusted operating income, which the speaker did not define. The contract flags this correctly.

evidence.note: FT, Sept 14: shareholders were told Q3 adjusted operating income would be positive, excluding stock compensation. This supports only the use of an adjusted measure. It does not show an unadjusted loss, concealment, or deterioration.
The exclusions it describes belong to the separate gross-margin figure. They cannot be transferred to adjusted operating income.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows Anthropic told investors to expect a Q3 profit on an adjusted basis that excludes stock compensation. No Q3 reconciliation or unadjusted result is in the packet, and nothing shows the adjustment was hidden. The support condition (excluding material expenses and obscuring that) is therefore not established, and the contradiction condition is not met either. The 'worse' part is hedged and not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase that keeps 'basically'. It is a firm but hyperbolic observation. The next sentence (not in 'the same universe of scale') suggests he means meaningful relative to capex.

contract.note: An absolute 'substantial revenue' reading is an ordinary plain reading. But the speaker himself cites billion-scale run rates at Cursor and Cognition, so a reading relative to capex may better match his intent; the contract flags this. The Apr–Jun period was chosen by the evaluator. Different readings could produce different outcomes.

evidence.note: Company disclosure of a $1B annualized run rate on Sept 25. It is a run rate outside the target quarter, not realized Apr–Jun revenue, and it is a self-report. It is relevant context against an absolute reading but cannot decide the contract.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires realized Apr–Jun 2026 revenue across the AI-native population. The packet holds only one September run-rate figure from a company disclosure. Under the contract's metric that figure cannot show substantial realized revenue, and it gives no broad coverage that could show near-absence. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron asserts the figure in his own voice. It appears to come from a Goldman Sachs sensitivity chart, which he presents and endorses as the answer.

semantics.note: Keeps the break-even case, the 10% operating margin, through-2027 capex and the ~$425B figure. Omits the training-cost inclusion, which the contract restores. The section heading says ~$400B, which is consistent with 'around'.

contract.note: It fairly checks whether the cited model yields ~$425B at a 10% margin under break-even. It does not test real outcomes, which is appropriate.

reviews.rationale: The Goldman report could not be read and no independent reproduction is in the packet. The speaker's own article cannot verify itself. With no evidence of what the model shows, the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own claim. Only the 'can't plug in' phrase is attributed to Nadella. The aggregate hoarding assertion is his.

semantics.note: The revised proposition keeps both branches, the named firms, 'far too many other companies', and the hundreds-of-billions scale.

contract.note: Reading 'hundreds of billions' as at least $200B in aggregate, valued at acquisition cost, is ordinary. The Apr–Jun period is the evaluator's choice for an ongoing-state claim, which is reasonable. The open population of other companies is flagged.

evidence.note: Secondary report (Oct 24) of Amazon warehousing about $5B of GB300 racks in August, plus about $3B a month after that. It covers one company, a period after the target quarter, and purchase flows. It does not measure the aggregate stock.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence shows that one company stored undeployed hardware after the target quarter, worth billions rather than hundreds of billions. No aggregate valuation of unused chips across the named firms is in the packet. The claim is neither established nor refuted.
